items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend chapter 719 of the laws of 1982, relating to authorizing the
commissioner of general services to convey certain state lands in the county
of Suffolk to the town of Islip, in relation to exceptions for certain
property
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6437

SPONSOR: WEIK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend chapter 719 of the laws of 1982, relating to authorizing
the commissioner of general services to convey certain state lands in
the county of Suffolk to the town of Islip, in relation to exceptions
for certain property

 
PURPOSE:

To permit the Town of Islip to sell and convey certain parcels of land
without the use restrictions in the enabling legislation of chapter 719
of the laws of 1982.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1-Section 1 amends chapter 719 of the laws of 1982 to create a
new section 1-b which authorizes the town of Islip to sell and convey a
parcel of land.

Section 2-Section 2 amends chapter 719 of the laws of 1982 to create a
new sections 8-b and 8c which outlines the parcel of land at issue and
directs that the use restrictions on the property do not apply to this
referenced parcel.

Section 3-Section 3 sets forth an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 1982, the State conveyed the Central Islip Psychiatric Hospital to
the town of Islip (Islip), with several use restrictions on what the
parcels of land could be used for, including a municipal corporation or
a not-for-profit college or university (Chapter 719, Laws of 1982). In
1985, pursuant to the 1982 Statute, Islip transferred the property to
the New York Institute of Technology (NYIT). In 1996, Islip received
back several acres of undeveloped property, which still had the use
restrictions of the 1982 Statute (Subject Property).

Eventually, NYIT decided to sell portions the property. In order to
complete the sale, legislation was passed in 2001 to lift the 1982 Stat-
ute use restrictions (Chapter 269, Laws of 2001). Further sales of the
remaining portions of the NYIT property lifting the use restrictions was
done in 2013 (Chapter 498, Laws of 2013). However, because Islip had
already received back the Subject Property in 1996, that parcel of land
still remained under the 1982 Statute use restrictions.

In 2020, Islip decided it wanted to sell the Subject Property as it
served no municipal purpose. Islip auctioned the Subject Property for
sale and eventually found a buyer; however, the parcel was still subject
to the use restrictions from 1982. On April 20, 2021, Islip passed a
unanimous resolution requesting that the use restrictions on the Subject
Property be lifted (Town of Islip Resolution  26, 4/20/21). Accordingly,
this legislation is necessary to effectuate the desire of Islip by lift-
ing the use restrictions on the Subject Property.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.
